The 20x figure is accurate, but calling it "fairly priced" distorts historical context. The 10-year average Forward P/E is ~18x, while the 25-year average sits around 16.5x. "The average bull market lasts 5.5 years and yields 265%, so we have plenty of room to grow." PARTIALLY TRUE/FALSE
The historical numbers are correct, but treating historical averages as a guarantee for the current rally is a fallacy. Market cycles do not follow rigid countdown timers or mandatory gain quotas.

"Nasdaq gained 600% during the Dot-Com era vs. only 150% in the current AI era, so there's no euphoria." PARTIALLY TRUE/FALSE
The percentages are correct, but comparing raw percentage gains ignores the massive dollar scale involved today. Adding 150% to today's multi-trillion-dollar companies represents vastly more absolute capital than the entire market cap of the late 1990s.

"87% of S&P 500 companies beat earnings, showing the rally is driven by strong fundamentals across all sectors." MOSTLY TRUE
